note: Bellmead, TX -- the five Euclidean base districts whose ordinance sections state a numeric yard block, read from the Bellmead Zoning Ordinance (the separate numbered ordinance printed as Sections I-XXIII, not the base Code of Ordinances chapters). ROUTE: Bellmead publishes this zoning ordinance on its site as a list of Municode nodeIds; library.municode.com/tx/bellmead is the official home but a plain fetch of the Municode ordinance pages returns a JavaScript shell with no server-rendered text, so Municode could NOT be read on this pass and is NOT the source of any value here. The text was read instead on Zoneomics (.../bellmead-TX/chapter_N, one page per ordinance section number: chapter_4 = Section IV districts, chapter_5 = Section V R-1, chapter_6 = Section V.1 R-1A, chapter_7 = Section V.2 parking, chapter_8 = Section VI R-2, chapter_9 = Section VII B-1, chapter_10 = Section VIII B-2, chapter_11 = Section IX I), which reproduces the ordinance text including each section's codification-history line. That is a rendered-page read of a live third-party mirror of the city's own ordinance; the mirror is live and fetchable, not a dead or stale document, but it is a mirror and not the city's Municode product. VINTAGE: Section V (R-1) carries the codification history '(Ord. of 9-10-63, Sec. 1; Ord. No. 2001-001, Sec. 1, 1-8-02; Ord. No. 2013-002 (5-14-13), Sec. 1, 5-14-13; Ord. No. 2025-005, Sec. 2, 6-10-2025)', so the R-1 dimensional block is current through Ordinance 2025-005, adopted 6-10-2025, and the ordinance itself dates to 9-10-1963 -- both read at source. The equivalent history lines for Sections VI, VII, VIII and IX were not captured verbatim in this pass, so no per-section amendment date is asserted for those four rows; the text quoted for them is the text the mirror serves today. OMITTED: R-1A (Section V.1). Section V.1 states use regulations only -- it lists permitted uses ('any use permitted in the R-1 District' plus duplex and two-family dwellings) and a carport restriction, and contains no height, yard, lot-area or coverage subsection at all. The section defers to nothing. Rather than interpolate R-1's numbers into R-1A, that district is left out with the gap recorded here (the same omit-rather-than-invent handling cibolo-tx.json uses for its SF-5/SF-6). USE-KEYED YARDS, NOT DISTRICT-KEYED: B-1, B-2 and I do not state one yard block per district. B-1 and B-2 give R-2-permitted uses the R-2 yard rules and give their own additional (commercial) uses different ones; I gives R-2-permitted uses the B-2 front yard and requires no front/side/rear yard of its other uses. This table codes the NON-RESIDENTIAL / 'other uses' branch as the district's base number, because that is the branch that governs the use class the district exists to serve, and quotes the use-keyed clause verbatim in every such field at reduced confidence. Anyone reading these rows for a residential use inside a B-1/B-2/I district must use the R-2 row instead. PROPORTIONAL STANDARDS: R-2's side yard is 'not less than ten (10) percent of the width of the lot, but such side yard need not exceed five (5) feet and shall not be less than four (4) feet', and its rear yard is 'at least twenty-five (25) percent of the depth of the lot but such depth need not be more than twenty-five (25) feet'. Neither is a scalar. Both are coded at the stated floor/cap figure with not_specified true and the full proportional clause quoted, following the batch-2 method (a proportion is not a scalar and must not be coded as if it were). NO COVERAGE STANDARD EXISTS in this ordinance -- not lot coverage and not impervious cover -- for any of the five districts coded here; every coverage field is a not_specified sentinel with that search result stated. R-1 is the only district in the whole ordinance with a lot-area/width rule (7,700 sq ft and 70 ft average width, Section V(D)), and that is not one of the seven coded fields.

front_ft.quote: Front yard. The minimum front yard setback shall be twenty-five feet (25').

rear_ft.quote: Rear yard. The minimum rear yard setback shall be thirty feet (30').

side_ft.quote: Side yards. The minimum side yard setback shall be five feet (5').

side_corner_ft.quote: Section V(C) states front, side and rear yards only and no separate corner-lot or street-side side yard figure.

max_height_ft.quote: Height regulations: No building shall exceed two and one-half (2 1/2) stories or thirty-five (35) feet in height except as provided in Section XI hereof. -- 35 ft is stated directly; the stories figure is not a conversion.

max_lot_coverage_pct.quote: Bellmead's zoning ordinance (Sections I-XXII of the appendix to the Code of Ordinances, as read) contains no impervious-coverage standard at all, and no lot-coverage percentage either: its district sections regulate height, yards and (for R-1) lot area/width only.

max_impervious_pct.quote: Bellmead's zoning ordinance (Sections I-XXII of the appendix to the Code of Ordinances, as read) contains no impervious-coverage standard at all, and no lot-coverage percentage either: its district sections regulate height, yards and (for R-1) lot area/width only.

front_ft.quote: Yard regulations: [Front yard.] There shall be a front yard along the front line of the lot. The minimum depth of such front yard shall be twenty-five (25) feet.

rear_ft.quote: Rear yard. The depth of the rear yard shall be at least twenty-five (25) percent of the depth of the lot but such depth need not be more than twenty-five (25) feet. -- a proportion with a cap, not a scalar; 25 (the stated cap) is coded and flagged, do not read it as a flat 25 ft rear yard.

side_ft.quote: Side yards. There shall be a side yard on each side of a building of not less than ten (10) percent of the width of the lot, but such side yard need not exceed five (5) feet and shall not be less than four (4) feet. -- a proportion with a ceiling and a floor, not a scalar; 4 (the stated floor) is coded and flagged, the ceiling being 5 ft and the general rule being 10% of lot width.

side_corner_ft.quote: Section VI(C) states front, side and rear yards only and no separate corner-lot or street-side side yard figure.
